content: 1. Administer 5 mg of the medication daily for regular use, or a 10 mg dose every 72 hours for as-needed use. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 2. Tipranavir reduces the effectiveness of tamoxifen by decreasing its metabolism. This occurs due to its impact on hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme activity. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Tecovirimat reduces the levels or effects of tipranavir by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 6. Tipranavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if coadministered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. Monitor therapy closely. 9. Tipranavir increases levels of ticagrelor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of timolol by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tipranavir increases levels of tisotumab vedotin by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE and the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Tipranavir increases levels of toremifene by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Metabolism of toremifene may be inhibited by drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 hepatic enzymes. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of tramadol by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ublituximab reduces the effects of tipranavir due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate; coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 19. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution if upadacitinib is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 21. Tipranavir and venlafaxine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Tipranavir increases venlafaxine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Tipranavir also increases verapamil levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates; coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 24. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of warfarin by an unspecified mechanism. Monitor INR more frequently if coadministered with inhibitors of CYP3A4, CYP1A2, or CYP2C19 isoenzymes, and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 27. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Reduce zanubrutinib to 80 mg once daily if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. Resume the previous zanubrutinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 29. Tipranavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tipranavir decreases zidovudine levels by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of amphetamine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 33. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 34. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of chlorpromazine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of codeine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Danazol increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 38. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of dexfenfluramine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of dextromethorphan by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of donepezil by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 42. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of doxepin by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of encainide by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 45. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 46. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of fluphenazine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ganaxolone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Changes in ganaxolone exposures when coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. 48. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ixazomib by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Clinical trials indicate no meaningful change in systemic exposure to ixazomib when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 49. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of loratadine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 50. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of perhexiline by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 51. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of perphenazine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 52. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of prochlorperazine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 53. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of promazine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 54. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of promethazine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of risperidone by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 56. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of tramadol by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 58. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of trifluoperazine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 59. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of tropisetron by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 60. Tipranavir decreases levels of abacavir by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, requiring dose reduction. Resume the previous abemaciclib dose after discontinuing the strong inhibitor. 62. Tipranavir increases levels of acalabrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong inhibitor is necessary, temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 63. Tipranavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. New onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Tipranavir increases levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. DM1, the cytotoxic component, is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Tipranavir decreases levels of afatinib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Increase the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg as tolerated if chronic therapy with a P-gp inducer is required. Resume the previous afatinib dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the P-gp inducer. 66. Tipranavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through an unspecified mechanism. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors exist. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Tipranavir increases levels of alfentanil by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Tipranavir increases levels of alfuzosin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 69. Tipranavir increases levels of alprazolam by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 70. Tipranavir increases levels of amiodarone by decreasing its metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 71. Tipranavir increases levels of amlodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 72. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Tipranavir increases levels of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III through pharmacodynamic synergism. Tipranavir has mild antiplatelet activity, which may increase bleeding risk. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Tipranavir increases levels of apalutamide by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of tipranavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
